_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: It is a classical guitar waltz.
beats.note: Gran Vals, composed in 1902 by the Spanish guitarist Francisco Tarrega. Nokia used a short phrase from early in the piece.
Anssi Vanjoki found the piece and showed it to Lauri Kivinen. Yle describes them as Nokia's sales and marketing director and its communications director.

beats.text: It first rang on the Nokia 2110.
beats.note: BGR says the phone listed it as Ringtone Type 7.

beats.text: A guitarist from Turku recorded it.
beats.note: Yle reports that Timo Korhonen was paid a fee and given his own Nokia 2110, and later regretted not asking for more.

beats.text: It was Grande Valse before it was Nokia tune.
beats.note: The Grande Valse name arrived in 1997 and Nokia tune in 1998, according to both Wikipedia and BGR.

beats.text: A guitar waltz from 1902 became the sound of Nokia.

beats.line: Hum it. You already know it.
